title: Two under-threshold wires -- the second wire's correction word arrives in a separate finalized turn (hand-built, live finding)
description: Hand-built from run 34's live transcript (report scripts/rehearse/reports/2026-09-11T22-48-44-structuring-two-wires.md): identical to structuring-two-wires.json except AssemblyAI's endpointing finalized the scripted line "Actually, there's a second one too -- $42,300 to the same account, same vendor." as TWO caller turns (c8a at 9500ms, c8b at 9800ms) with no agent turn between them, instead of one. Live, that split let the amount-bearing turn grade CONTRADICTED instead of CORRECTED (see ledger.test.ts test 10 for the direct, isolated proof of that classification, and the ledger.ts fix comment for the mechanism); combined with the already-failing context check, the live call FROZE mid-call (row 8) before the agent's follow-up readback and the caller's confirming "Yes, that's right." ever happened. This recording, unlike the live call, includes that eventual confirming readback and reply (c10/c11, same as the baseline scenario) -- once the caller reconfirms the new amount, its claim is marked CONFIRMED regardless of what it graded a moment earlier, which is why this file's `expected` verdict is ESCALATE (matching structuring-two-wires.json exactly) with or without the ledger.ts fix applied. Its purpose is G3 end-to-end coverage that this realistic split-turn transcript variant still reaches the scenario's correct final verdict -- it is deliberately NOT the regression test for the fix itself (a full completed call can't isolate a transient mid-call misclassification once a later readback overwrites it); ledger.test.ts test 10 is.
